title: Postoperative Respiratory Care (Abdominal and Thoracic Surgery)
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Type of surgery and incision; analgesia (epidural, patient-controlled); drains, lines, catheters; surgical restrictions; pre-operative mobility; smoking; lung disease; pain level.
working: Postoperative Respiratory Care (Abdominal and Thoracic Surgery)
qa: Why are upper abdominal operations high risk? Pain and diaphragm dysfunction reduce lung volumes.
What is the single most important postoperative intervention? Early mobilisation.
Why support the wound during cough? Reduces pain and allows a stronger cough.
Where should a chest drain bottle be kept? Below the level of the chest.
When does physiotherapy start for planned major surgery? Before surgery, with education and fitness.

redFlags.Finding: Rising RR, fever, new crackles or bronchial breathing
Low BP, high HR, increased drain output or wound bleeding
Air leak increasing, subcutaneous emphysema, sudden breathlessness with chest drain
redFlags.Action: Medical team; do not clamp drains

manualNotes: Chest drains: keep the drainage bottle below chest level, never lift above the patient, do not clamp unless instructed, watch for swinging and bubbling as instructed.
